17531199_1b2c859c.text: The GABAergic neurons that comprise the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) surround and inhibit the neurons in the thalamic relay nuclei (Steriade et al., 1997;(Crabtree, 1999). TRN neurons often participate in widespread rhythmic, synchronized activity that encompasses other thalamic nuclei and the neocortex (Steriade et al., 1987)(Krosigk et al., 1993)

17531199_381d9a14.text: .Axons originating outside the TRN, such as glutamatergic afferents from the neocortex and thalamic relay nuclei, may help to synchronize the firing of TRN cells (Destexhe et al., 1998)(Bal et al., 2000)(Blumenfeld et al., 2000). Synaptic connectivity within the TRN is also likely to play an important role. Anatomical (Deschenes et al., 1985;Yen et al., 1985;De Biasi et al., 1988;Liu and Jones, 1999) and physiological (Ulrich and Huguenard, 1996;Sanchez-Vives et al., 1997;Shu and McCormick, 2002) evidence suggest that TRN neurons form mutually inhibitory GABAergic synapses.
